title: The new FiberSteel Boat Lifts website

scenes.narration: This is a concept for the new FiberSteel Boat Lifts website. It opens with what FiberSteel builds, both phone lines, and whether the office is open right now.
Lifts are picked by boat: personal watercraft, V-bottoms, pontoons, performance boats, large cruisers, front-mounted and shallow water.
Each boat type has its own page, with FiberSteel's photos, the sizes that fit, and how the lift is set up for that boat.
The sizes page lists every standard lift, with its arms, axles and poly tanks.
And the calculator uses FiberSteel's own formula: the boat's dry weight, plus its fuel, plus two thousand pounds, or three thousand for boats over thirty feet.
The answer carries straight into a quote request, with the boat already filled in.
Next comes the slip: its width and length, and how the boat docks.
Then a name, and a phone number or an email.
Sending it emails the request to the address FiberSteel chooses, for the team to review.
The pages owners know from the current site are all here too, just modernized.
Admiral remote systems, with the prices from the current site.
Used lifts, first come, first served. The listings in this demo are samples.
Every authorized dealer is listed here, with a filter by state.
Help for owners: service and parts, the warranty, FiberSteel's guides, and its videos.
The warranty, in plain words: lifetime on the poly tanks and the frame.
And the contact page, with both lines, the hours, and directions to the shop in Camdenton.
The lake info, the lakefront rental and the electric bikes are still here too, out of the way in the footer.
That's the new FiberSteel website. The installs showcase has its own short video.
